body:
For the record, I believe everyone is entitled to their beliefs.  What I
don't appreciate are hypocritical smears and intimidation.  People should be
able to express their views without apprehension that they might say the
wrong thing.

That said, I think it's great that David Duke is running for Congress.  I
don't like him personally, but at least he is something different.  I would
be just as pleased to see a Marxist or socialist running for Congress, to be
honest.  I want to see diversity.  I yearn for the days of nationalism,
especially.  Centrism spoils the party when there is too much of it.  Some
may argue that it brings stability to the nation, but let's face it, there
are some consequences.  (Well, that's another topic.)

I don't appreciate the clustering of me with David Duke.  Of course, it's
inevitable given the shift to the left that has occured since the '60s.
Anything that is different is bound to be labelled an -ist something, either
implicitly or explicitly.  But that's okay, I've gotten used to it, plus
those lame pejoratives have lost the sting they once had! ;o)

I'm also sick of crackers like that lady on Newsweek who contributes for the
McGlaughlin Group on PBS, who spew centrist, liberal, do-gooder garbage.  I
can just imagine the suburban house she lives in; it's gotta be huge!  It
takes someone who's really good at not offending anyone to make it as far
within the media as she has, I would guess (maybe I'm wrong, oh well, just
intuition.)

Getting back to the topic, I hate the KKK.  They are illiterate and have
absolutely NO class.  Basically, what they do is carry around Bibles and use
their religion to condone racism (or whatever else they believe.. incest?).
I am atheist; they think I'm going to hell.

David Duke and his degenerate, freckled face, barbarian-descended clones
wouldn't last a day in Madrid or Barcelona.  The Falangists would easily
kick their pale asses, and drive them to the Pyrenees!  Anti-Catholic punks.
Those people need to learn some history.  If it wasn't for the Roman emperor
Constantine there wouldn't even be any protestant sects.  People would still
be pagans, I suppose.


Well, I found some interesting quotes:

[Note: I am not a Satanist, but think some of the beliefs of those "new
agers" to be intruiguing.]

"Recently we have seen certain evangelists and even academics calling
Satanism a neo-Nazi movement. This is an innacurate label. The Nazi movement
drew much of its power from a racist doctrine of Aryan superiority. Satanism
is far more discerning than that. While there are provable biological
differences between the races and statistically demonstrable performance
levels in various activities, it is quite irrational to think that someone
can be elite or not simply because of the color of their skin. Even if one
comes from promising genetic stock, and by that we mean from ancestors who
have proven their abilities to be superior in performance, this does not
guarantee an individual's advancement. No, we Satanists only recognize an
individual as elite if they prove it by cultivating their abilities to the
highest extent possible. This is something that requires the Satanic virtue
of discipline, a quality we try to instill in our own iron youth. There are
elite individuals from all ethnic backgrounds, and they are embraced by
Satanism for the superior beings that they are."

-- Peter Gilmore, Magister of the Church of Satan

"Those who are most sensitive about "politically incorrect" terminology are
not the average black ghetto-dweller, Asian immigrant, abused woman or
disabled person, but a minority of activists, many of whom do not even
belong to any "oppressed" group but come from privileged strata of society.
Political correctness has its stronghold among university professors, who
have secure employment with comfortable salaries, and the majority of whom
are heterosexual, white males from middle-class families. "

-- Ted Kaczynski (paragraph 12)
